teachers.title: Teaching GRAFCET and ladder logic with Studomate
teachers.intro: Studomate is a free GRAFCET, ladder logic and HMI simulator that runs in the browser. It is used to prepare, hand out and mark automation lab exercises, in vocational and technical programmes (BTS CRSA, BTS ATI, BTS Électrotechnique, bac pro MELEC, STI2D, BUT GEII) and in engineering schools.

sections.title: Preparing a lab exercise
items: Start from a ready-made project: traffic light, crossroads, car park barrier, elevator, drilling or carton sorting. Each comes in an exercise version and a solution version.
Write the exercise statement in Markdown in the project properties: it travels with the project and opens in a tab.
Keep the solution in a separate project that you do not share.

sections.title: Handing the project out to students
items: From your account, share a link: each student who opens it gets their own copy, without creating an account. The link can be revoked at any time.
Or send a project file, which students open in Studomate.

sections.title: Nothing for students to install
items: Studomate runs in the browser: nothing to install on the lab computers or at students' homes.
Without an account, projects stay in the student's browser. An account, with or without an email address, saves them to the cloud.
No tracking cookies, and free software under the AGPL v3 licence.

sections.title: Collecting and marking the work
items: Each student sends you back a project file, or a share link to their copy.
The analyser reports the project's errors (invalid expression, unknown variable...) before simulation.
The project PDF export gives a cover page with the exercise statement, then the grafcets, the ladders and the variable tables: a basis for the lab report.

sections.title: Going further
items: Connect the program to a 3D carton-sorting scene, driven by its outputs.
Load the program onto a real Arduino Uno R3 board, or use its inputs and outputs during simulation (Chrome or Edge).

teachers.trainingBody: The training follows a six-module progression, from basic logic to implementing a GRAFCET in ladder logic. Each module alternates theory and solved exercises to simulate, and the glossary defines every term.

faq.question: Does Studomate replace TIA Portal, Automgen or CODESYS?
faq.answer: No, and that is not its purpose. Studomate is for learning and practice: it simulates GRAFCET, ladder logic and HMI pages in the browser. It does not program an industrial PLC (Siemens, Schneider…), though it can drive an Arduino board. In class it complements the software of the workshop's PLC: students design and test their logic in Studomate, in the lab or at home, then carry it over to the real hardware. The notations follow the standards: IEC 60848 for GRAFCET, IEC 61131-3 blocks (TON, TOF, CTU…) for ladder logic.

faq.question: Can students practise at home without PLC software?
faq.answer: Yes. Studomate is free and runs in the browser with no installation, on Windows, macOS or Linux. A student can redo a lab exercise or follow the course on their own computer, with no licence and no hardware.

faq.question: Does anything need to be installed on the lab computers?
faq.answer: No. A recent browser is enough. Only using an Arduino board requires Chrome or Edge.

faq.question: Do students need to create an account?
faq.answer: No. Without an account, they open the shared project and work in their browser. An account, with or without an email address, lets them find their projects on another device and share their own by link.

faq.question: Is Studomate free to use in class?
faq.answer: Yes, in class as at home. The code is free software under the AGPL v3 licence.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.purposeBody: These terms govern access to and use of Studomate, a teaching application dedicated to learning, designing and simulating automated systems. The tool provides interactive spaces to represent, simulate and understand the various languages, diagrams and logic of industrial automation. By accessing Studomate, the user acknowledges having read and accepted these terms.
terms.usageBody: Studomate is designed for supervised educational and professional use: teaching, training, self-learning or technical demonstration. The user agrees to:
usageItems: use the platform in compliance with the law and the rights of others;
not misuse the application for unlawful, commercial or malicious purposes;
not modify or attempt to access the source code without authorisation;
credit Studomate in any public use that incorporates it.
terms.accountsBody: The current version of Studomate requires no sign-up. Projects and simulations are stored locally in files. The user is responsible for backing up their files. No personal data is sent to external servers without explicit consent.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.introBody: This privacy policy describes how Studomate handles users' personal and technical data. It aims to ensure transparency and to spell out the privacy choices available.
privacy.collectedBody: Studomate collects no identifying personal data automatically. By default, the projects a user creates are stored locally in their browser and are sent to no remote server. Data leaves the user's device in only two cases, described below: audience measurement (§3) and, if they choose to create an account, accounts and cloud backup (§4).
privacy.analyticsBody: Studomate uses Umami (hosted in the European Union) to measure site traffic: number of visits, pages viewed, traffic sources, device type, and a few anonymous usage events (creating a project, starting a simulation). These measurements are taken without cookies, without storing the IP address and without any way to identify or track a user from one visit to the next. No data is sold or used for advertising.
privacy.accountsBody: Creating an account is optional: without an account, Studomate runs entirely locally and no data is sent to our servers. By creating an account, a user can back up their projects to the cloud and access them on another device.
accountsItems: Anonymous account: nickname and password, no email address.
Data stored: an account identifier, the email or nickname, and only the projects the user chooses to save to the cloud.
privacy.accountsHosting: This data is hosted by our processor Supabase, on infrastructure located in the European Union. Each account can access only its own data (isolation enforced at the database level). No data is sold or used for advertising.
privacy.securityBody: Studomate is committed to a high level of data protection and to never exploiting data for commercial or advertising purposes. Exchanges with the cloud are encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and access to saved projects is restricted to the account that created them. Users remain responsible for the security of files they export locally.
privacy.cookiesBody: Studomate uses no tracking cookies. Only technical data is stored locally for projects to work correctly (internal identifiers, simulation states, saved settings).
privacy.rightsBody: In accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), any user may:
rightsItems: erase the local data in their browser at any time;
export or manually back up their projects at any time;
request deletion of their account and associated projects by contacting the team (§8).

theory-structure.description: Split a Ladder program into subprograms: the Main program calls one subprogram per machine function, so each part stays readable.

exercise-subprograms.title: Calling a ladder logic subprogram: exercise
exercise-subprograms.description: A conveyor whose Main does not call the counting subprogram yet: add the call and check it in simulation, in a self-corrected exercise.

synthesis-packing.title: Batch case packing in ladder logic: exercise
synthesis-packing.description: Count parts on a conveyor and pack them in batches of 5 into cases, with a ladder logic program structured in subprograms: a corrected assignment.

conclusion.title: Module A3 conclusion: Studomate and the standard
conclusion.description: Module A3 recap: timers, counters, numeric values and how to structure a Ladder program into subprograms.

exercise-grafcet-naive.title: GRAFCET in ladder logic: flaws of the naive method
exercise-grafcet-naive.description: Diagnose in simulation a common but flawed way of implementing a GRAFCET in ladder logic, the next-step method, and understand its flaws.

theory-method-ladder.title: From GRAFCET to Ladder: one network per transition
theory-method-ladder.description: Implement a GRAFCET in Ladder: one network per transition (upstream reset, downstream set), order of the networks and activation of the initial step.

theory-two-programs.title: Two Ladder programs for a GRAFCET: training
theory-two-programs.description: Arrange a GRAFCET implemented in Ladder into two programs, Automatic_cycle and Outputs, called by the Main: a complete example and a checklist.

exercise-grafcet-linear.title: Linear GRAFCET sequence in ladder logic: exercise
exercise-grafcet-linear.description: Implement the GRAFCET of a linear sequence in ladder logic, with one network per transition and the Automatic_cycle and Outputs programs.

theory-actions-ladder.title: Continuous and stored actions in ladder logic: training
theory-actions-ladder.description: Implement a GRAFCET's continuous, stored and conditional actions in Ladder: one network per output, in the Outputs program.

theory-edge-actions-ladder.title: Edge and numeric actions in ladder logic: training
theory-edge-actions-ladder.description: Implement a GRAFCET's edge actions in Ladder with P and N contacts, and numeric assignments, on a car-counting example.

theory-receptivity-timer.title: Timed transition condition in ladder logic: training
theory-receptivity-timer.description: Place the TON of a timed transition condition in the transition's network, and delay or limit an output with a step and a timed transition.

theory-movement-supervision.title: Supervising a movement in ladder logic: training
theory-movement-supervision.description: Supervise a movement with a TON and a fallback transition, latch the fault in the Faults program and acknowledge it without clearing it if the cause persists.

synthesis-drilling.title: Drilling station, from GRAFCET to ladder: exercise
synthesis-drilling.description: Write the control part of a drilling station in ladder logic from its GRAFCET, against a simulated operative part: a corrected summary assignment.

conclusion.title: Module A4 conclusion: GRAFCET in Ladder, part 1
conclusion.description: Module A4 recap: steps as memories, network per transition, Automatic_cycle and Outputs programs, actions, time and faults of a GRAFCET implemented in Ladder.

exercise-grafcet-or-divergence.title: GRAFCET OR divergence in ladder logic: exercise
exercise-grafcet-or-divergence.description: Implement a GRAFCET with an OR divergence and convergence in ladder logic: a choice between two sequences depending on the button pressed.

theory-and-divergence-ladder.title: AND divergence and convergence in ladder logic: training
theory-and-divergence-ladder.description: Implement a GRAFCET's AND divergence and convergence in Ladder: a single network for the divergence and a single one for the convergence.

exercise-grafcet-and-divergence.title: GRAFCET AND divergence in ladder logic: exercise
exercise-grafcet-and-divergence.description: Implement a GRAFCET with an AND divergence and convergence in ladder logic: two actions launched in parallel, then synchronised again.

theory-grafcet-reset.title: Stopping a GRAFCET sequence in ladder logic: training
theory-grafcet-reset.description: The two ways of stopping a sequence in Ladder: immediate stop by reinitialisation and end-of-cycle stop, and where to place the reset network.

exercise-grafcet-reset.title: Traffic light with stops in ladder logic: exercise
exercise-grafcet-reset.description: Implement a traffic light GRAFCET in ladder logic, then add an immediate stop and an end-of-cycle stop to it: a self-corrected exercise.

synthesis-parking.title: Car park, from GRAFCET to ladder logic: exercise
synthesis-parking.description: Implement in ladder logic the GRAFCET of a 4-space car park with a barrier, a space counter and a "full" indicator: a corrected summary assignment.

theory-going-further.title: Limits of one network per transition: training
theory-going-further.description: When one network per transition reaches its limit (one press read by several transitions), on a single-button remote gate example.

theory-three-blocks.title: The three-block method in ladder logic: training
theory-three-blocks.description: The three-block method to implement a GRAFCET in Ladder: crossing conditions, all the resets then all the sets, then the outputs.

conclusion.title: Module A5 conclusion: GRAFCET in Ladder, part 2
conclusion.description: Module A5 recap: OR and AND divergences, stopping a sequence, the car park's programs and the limits of one network per transition.
